# Requirements and domain truth

Use only for the `requirements` TODO section. Produce the accepted backend dependency PRD and freeze domain facts before capability discovery. Do not load model, apply, verification, or acceptance authority at this stage.

## Backend dependency PRD

Preserve the full accepted product demand as the requirements baseline. For a new project, complete replacement, or existing project increment, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`, or record an equivalent traceable current-batch delta that references the unchanged accepted baseline. Never silently reduce product demand to an MVP.

One Delivery Batch may implement an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Record its stable Requirement IDs, planned Feature keys, baseline delivery/model identity, allowed shared-resource changes and affected regression boundary. Requirements outside the batch remain explicit deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership; `done` closes only the batch. A Feature slice must be dependency-closed: include any shared Role, entrypoint, Object, Action, Report, lifecycle or authorization change required for its behavior to be valid and verifiable.

Settle domain truth completely for the current batch and dependency closure before capability discovery. Deferred slices need enough stable identity and ownership to remain visible, but their unresolved details do not block this batch unless they change its observable result, authorization, amount/unit semantics, irreversible effect, or state flow. A later batch reuses the accepted baseline and resolves its own delta instead of rewriting unrelated requirements.

A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as `<doc> §N`. If one section states a rule completely, cite it rather than restating it. A reference-mode PRD still carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section.

Read frontend evidence, when present, in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/handlers and fixtures/seeds; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Requirements inspection is read-only. Mock or visible behavior proves demand or a current assumption, not a business rule without higher-precedence evidence.

When the frontend is already implemented, do not stop at API method names or TypeScript types. Search for every API dependency's Mock implementation, including request handlers, success/error responses, fixture collections, seeded identities, mutation side effects, generated identifiers, relation keys, enum/status values, timestamps, totals, and nested objects. Reconcile those concrete values with component reads and writes. Add any evidenced missing object, field, relation, lifecycle state, query shape, or representative worked example to the PRD, with its exact source path and an appropriate classification. Preserve conflicts and optionality: Mock-only fields remain `recommended` or `open` unless higher-precedence evidence confirms them, and decorative/test-only values do not become domain facts.

Use this precedence while preserving every conflict:

1. explicit current user decision;
2. latest accepted requirement or design contract;
3. latest implemented frontend behavior;
4. typed API and Mock semantics;
5. frontend tests;
6. legacy/reference implementation.

Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract actors, journeys, observable success, objects, fields, relations, queries, commands, states, permissions/scopes, errors/conflicts, calculations, transactions/idempotency, external effects, and presentation-only behavior. Every write operation names authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof.

Build one traceability row per in-scope requirement: `demand evidence → requirement ID → Feature key → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Account for every backend-bound typed API operation and route touched by the batch; reference the accepted baseline for unchanged rows and preserve explicit dispositions for deferred rows. Matrix cells are phrases; do not repeat table facts in prose.

## Critical ambiguity

Classify every unresolved choice before capability selection. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring, and only for the smallest affected slice.

| Decision class | Boundary | Handling | Blocks model? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `business_blocker` | At least two concrete incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the choices, affected requirements/model items, and obtain current user or accepted requirement authority | Yes, smallest slice only |
| `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal code, canonical identity/context source, or accepted-fact-to-capability mapping | Defer discovery to the typed client/fixed capability contract; record a Foundation/Runtime gap if absent | No |
| `safe_implementation_decision` | Reversible technical choice preserving the accepted invariant | Defer to the published standard or record one conservative default and evolution path | No |
| `product_follow_up` | Product preference with a fallback that preserves required results | Record assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger | No |

Security/privacy omissions default to least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export. An explicit broader-disclosure requirement remains a `business_blocker` until its authorization boundary is confirmed.

Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules:

- Explicit exact decimals, comparisons, or sums do not require absent optional currency/unit/range metadata; block only a comparison/conversion slice where incompatible units change the required result.
- Explicit asynchronous approval may use an independent approval Object while the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect; missing edit/cancel/resubmit preferences are follow-ups.
- An explicitly immutable resource with no required business-role read needs no invented read actor; prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence.
- Weekday/morning intent with no timezone/holiday preference uses deterministic deployment timezone and standard weekday cron; block only explicit incompatible calendar outcomes.

## Domain truth design

Freeze domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement. When requirements contain calculations, historical facts, settlement, correction, or reversal, read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) once and close its ownership, persistence, snapshot, trace, correction, and consumer decisions.

Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, define the write-side atomic action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its reports.

Before capability discovery, settle only the model-visible Report facts: the business question, Object SQL source of truth, parameters and defaults, result columns and meanings, authorization/audience, and whether export is required. Report query transport and export execution are Runtime-owned and stay out of the project model and PRD.

Every required Report export defaults to an offline Data Exchange job. When the project owns a frontend, the PRD also records the export-center route/audience and the actor-visible job-list/download outcome. If the active typed Runtime Client lacks the actor-owned Data Exchange export-job list, record a Data Exchange owner gap instead of inventing a route or browser-local list.

Verify the authorized Object SQL result, out-of-scope denial, offline job submission, actor-owned job-list visibility, and completed-file download when export is required. Do not turn Runtime execution internals into project acceptance cases.

Record any explicitly required current-database query-plan evidence and driver (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, or `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`) as a business-flow verification obligation. Capability schemas are resolved during model routing; do not manufacture a separate platform gate catalog or case inventory.

```

- `!` means required.
- A default belongs in the base specification before the first modifier:
  `currency!=0;precision=19`, never `currency!;precision=19;=0`.
- `relation` requires `->target` and never accepts a default.
- `select` requires a non-empty, unique stable vocabulary. Labels default from
  the stable value when omitted.
- Supported non-relation Object modifiers are `unique`, `indexed`, `localized`,
  `min_length`, `max_length`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `precision`, `scale`,
  `currency`, `rounding`, `cardinality`, `on_delete`, `inverse`, `dictionary`,
  and `value_domain`.
- A relation never accepts `unique`; use `cardinality=one_to_one`, which makes
  the compiler derive uniqueness.
- Unknown types/modifiers, duplicates, invalid values, out-of-vocabulary
  defaults and context-inapplicable modifiers fail closed.
- Field types, modifier names and closed platform enum values are
  case-insensitive on input and compile to their documented lowercase values.
  ISO currency codes compile to uppercase. Stable business identities such as
  field keys, relation targets, option values, dictionaries and value domains
  remain strict lowercase identifiers.

Common repairs are local to the rejected field string:

| Rejected | Use | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"customer_id": "relation!"` | `"customer_id": "relation!->customer"` | A relation requires its target. |
| `"status": "select!"` | `"status": "select![draft\|done]"` | Select needs exactly one vocabulary source. |
| `"status": "select![draft];dictionary=status"` | Choose inline options or `dictionary`, not both. | Vocabulary sources are exclusive. |
| `"amount": "currency;precision=2;scale=3"` | `"amount": "currency;precision=19;scale=2"` | Scale cannot exceed precision. |
| `"amount": "currency!;precision=19;=0"` | `"amount": "currency!=0;precision=19"` | A default must precede every modifier. |
| `"starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03 09:00"` | `"starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03T09:00:00+08:00"` | Datetime defaults use RFC3339. |

The CLI rejects an invalid string during model loading and reports the stable
diagnostic code, exact JSON path, field key and repair facts. Fix that string;
do not replace the compact field map with generated full field arrays.

Notification variables use only the restricted `<type>[!]` subset. Their types
are `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `email`, `number`, `text`, and `url`; they do
not accept select options, relation targets, defaults, or modifiers. A business
enum such as `select![approved|rejected]` is rendered text in a notification, so
author it as `text!` and retain the enum on its owning Object or Action field.

Plane expands Object fields to `key`, `name`, `type`, `required`, `config`,
`validation`, labeled `options`, `unique` and `default_value`. Human-readable
names default from stable keys (`item_submission` -> `Item Submission`). Object
descriptions also receive a deterministic non-empty default; provide explicit
text only when it carries real domain meaning.

Action fields use the same strings. Object-only modifiers are consistency
assertions whose source Plane uniquely infers from the owning Object and the
Handler access closure, as detailed below. This preserves the named
type/precision contract without exposing source pointers to the model.

## Actions and source-owned Handlers

An Action key is exactly `<object_key>.<action_key>`; Plane derives
`object_key`, the default name, audit metadata, same-key Permission and empty
contracts. The model decides `kind`, allowed business roles, business fields,
preconditions and whether a source-owned Handler is needed.

`object_create` is the Runtime-owned generic single-Object create and must not
carry a project Handler. Use `object_operation` plus Handler/access when an
object-scoped create must derive trusted owner/org values, coordinate multiple
Objects, or execute other project logic. All other supported Handler kinds and
their object/record invocation scope are listed in the Actions capability
reference. A Handler Action must not use the bare suffix `create`, `read`,
`update`, `delete`, `restore`, `import`, or `export`, because those exact
`<object>.<operation>` keys belong to Runtime Object Permissions. Use a business
verb such as `lead.register` or a qualified key such as `lead.create_owned`;
grant that exact Action key to the Role.

```json
{
  "actions": {
    "invoice.approve": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "input": {"comment": "long_text!", "effective_date": "date!"},
      "output": {"status": "select![approved|rejected]"},
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Approval updates the invoice and durable decision atomically",
        "access": {
          "invoice": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
          "approval_decision": ["create"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`handler.reason` is the only authored capability-gap/rationale statement.
Plane derives owner, trigger, scope, atomicity, rollback semantics, involved
Objects, read/write sets and transaction requirement. Do not author
`authorization`, `payload_fields`, `handler.data_access`, `handler.output`,
`audit_event`, empty defaults, or behavior tuples.

An aggregate-only Handler may omit `access` when it declares
`cross_workspace_aggregates`; Plane emits empty raw `data_access` and derives
the fixed source Object into the read-effect closure. Use the
`cross-workspace-aggregate` reading topic for the closed dimensions, optional
source-owned date bucket, measures, filters, authorization, result schema, and
Runtime limit contract. Grain, IANA time zone, and Workspace selection are not
caller input.

A Handler may likewise omit `access` when its complete effect is expressed by
the narrow Foundation capabilities `target_organization`,
`store_organization_catalog`, `store_organization_mutations`,
`workspace_identity_usage`, or
`identity_handler_delivery`. These declarations compile into fixed generated
methods and descriptor grants; they do not authorize raw Object reads/writes or
generic Identity/Organization APIs. Load the `organization-delivery`,
`identity-handler-delivery`, or `workspace-identity-usage` reading topic before
authoring one of them. Identity/Profile mutation effects needed by a declared
profile binding are compiler-owned closure and must not be repeated as
`handler.access`.

Keep a plain Action-only value as a plain field DSL such as `"reason": "long_text"`;
it does not need a backing Object field. When an Action field
uses Object-only modifiers (for example `max_length`) or Object-backed numeric
semantics, Plane infers its source from the owning Object plus the Objects in
`handler.access`, using the Action field's exact key only. The owning Object wins
over an equally named field elsewhere in the access closure; equally ranked
same-key fields fail as ambiguous. Plane never binds differently named fields
through Action verbs, prefixes, suffixes, stemming, edit distance, grammar, or
synonyms. When an Action input and persisted Object field represent the same
business datum, give them the same stable key, for example
`rejection_reason` end to end. Otherwise remove Object-only modifiers to keep
the Action value standalone. The diagnostic lists compatible rename candidates
without choosing one. Never author a source pointer or add a fake Object field.
This source is generated type/lineage reuse only; it does not copy an Object
field's runtime value into the Action payload.

For `identity_handler_delivery`, keep Identity-owned, non-Profile inputs such
as `login_id`, `display_name`, `role_key`, and `manager` standalone: use plain
DSL such as `email!`, `text!`, `select![employee|manager]`, or `user`, without
Object-only modifiers. A Profile-bound value may reuse Object-only modifiers
only when the owning Object or an Object in `handler.access` has an exact
same-key compatible field. Read the `identity-handler-delivery` topic for a
complete Action input and Profile example; never add a fake Object field.

Two fixed Store Organization mutation inputs are the deliberate exception to
same-key Object source inference. For an exact `rename` grant,
`store_name: text!;max_length=200` and
`expected_store_version: integer!;min=1` belong to the Identity capability and
remain standalone. For `disable`, only `expected_store_version` is required.
Do not add either field to the business Object just to satisfy source inference.
Business state uses its own record CAS input and `conditional_update`; the two
version tokens are distinct and both mutations remain in one Runtime Action
transaction.

Do not put protocol or infrastructure identifiers in Action input: `id`,
`request_id`, `trace_id`, `correlation_id`, `idempotency_key`, `workspace_id`,
`principal_id`, `record_id`, `route_id`, `tenant_id`, `session_id`,
`database_id`, `db_id`, and `row_id` are rejected. Record targets come from the
Action route, idempotency from `Idempotency-Key`, request identity from Runtime,
and new technical IDs from backend code. Stable business numbers remain
legitimate business fields.

## Roles, data scope and write ownership

Roles contain exact Permission grants, and every grant carries its own scope:

```json
{"roles": {"reviewer": ["case.read;org", "case.approve;owner", "case_attachment.read;owner"]}}
```

The only scope values are `all`, `owner`, `org`, `org_child`, and
`target_org`. The Role's same-key Action Permission is the only authored
allowlist. Plane reverse-derives `authorization.allowed_roles`, registers the
Action Permission definition, and never invents a Role grant or scope. Authoring
`Action.roles` is rejected as a duplicate source.

Object write policy is compiler-owned:

- an Object written by a Handler is `action_only` and has no Runtime CRUD
  behavior;
- every other Object is `direct_crud` and receives a Runtime CRUD behavior;
- a direct create/update/delete/restore Role permission or entrypoint mutation
  on a Handler-written Object is a blocking ownership conflict.

Plane expands Role grants into one scoped data-permission container per declared Role/Object.
That container is compiler-owned: the model declares each exact
Permission and scope once as `roles.<role>[] = "<permission_key>;<data_scope>"` and never repeats the
expanded Object policy.

Never author `config.write_policy`, role-level `data_scope`, `scope_overrides`,
`data_permissions` or `reference_permissions`. Handler roles use their explicit
same-key Action grant without receiving direct CRUD mutation permissions.

## Relation reference input

A `relation->target` field is also the complete model input for a reusable
reference selector. Plane derives an exact reference policy only when the role
can write the source Object and read the target Object; duplicate
source/field/target policies collapse to one stable identity.

The frontend calls
`GET /records/{sourceObjectKey}/fields/{relationFieldKey}/options`
with the raw user `query`. It never supplies a target Object, display field,
permission, SQL wildcard or `LIKE` expression. Runtime resolves the relation,
enforces the reference and target row/field policies, escapes `%`, `_` and the
escape character, then creates a parameterized case-insensitive contains
predicate. The component renders only the returned `{"id":"…","name":"…"}`
items.

## Report SQL

Prefer one source-owned file instead of an escaped SQL string:

```json
{"reports": {
  "part_usage": {
    "audience_roles": ["report_reader"],
    "object_sql_v1": {
      "sql_file": "backend/reports/part_usage.sql",
      "parameters": {"status": "text!"}
    }
  }
}}
```

The path must be exactly `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`, canonical,
project-local and non-symlink. Plane normalizes line endings, hashes the source
and embeds SQL in the full Runtime contract. `sql_file` and `sql` are mutually
exclusive.

Plane derives the result schema and preserves SQL SELECT order. Optional
`result_schema` entries are semantic overrides keyed by SELECT alias and do not
control output ordering.

Quote every model-derived Object and field identifier with MySQL backticks,
including ``FROM `lead` l``, ``JOIN `order` o``, and qualified field references
such as ``l.`status```. This is mandatory even for ordinary stable keys: whether
the current parser treats a key as a keyword is not part of the authoring
contract. Keep aliases, parameter names, and result aliases as unquoted stable
keys.

Object SQL may reference only business fields explicitly declared under the
source Object's `fields`. Runtime-owned storage/scope columns
`owner_user_id`/`owner_org_id` are not project-declarable or Report-projectable
columns. Record-envelope `id` is available only as an internal JOIN, filter,
ordering, or COUNT operand and cannot be returned raw. Runtime applies owner/
organization permission scope before executing the Report. Every optional
`result_schema` entry overrides semantics for an existing SQL output alias.

Each `audience_roles` Role must grant `report.query.execute;all` as the exact
executable entry Permission, in addition to every source Object
`*.read;<requirement-selected-scope>` and required field-read policy. Audience
membership and source data access never authorize the Report query route by
themselves.

## Empty values and commands

Omit empty strings, arrays and objects. Omit absent `input`, `output`,
`permissions`, `config`, `preconditions` and optional collections; Plane
creates required empty internal structures. `false` and `0` remain legal only
when they are deliberate business values.

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <module> [--allow-destructive]
```

`model plan` is the no-HTTP repair loop. It runs the same loader, Ledger graph,
authoring checks, Project Contract projection, Runtime Manifest compiler and
source-owner validators used by apply. Its stdout `artifact` is a path relative
to the supplied `--project` root (also declared by
`artifact_relative_to: "--project"`), including on a non-zero repair result.
`apply model` atomically converges the
generated Ledger; an item absent from the model is a destructive deletion and
requires `--allow-destructive`.

Capability assembly remains progressive: choose from bounded summaries, load
only selected focused definitions, and let Plane compile ownership, module
closure and digests. Never author or cache a capability assembly in the model.

`templates/backend-model-handler-minimal/model.json.tmpl` is the directly
loadable two-Object Handler starter.

# Identity HandlerDelivery

Use `identity_handler_delivery` when one project-owned Action must create,
update, disable, or resolve an Identity user while binding it to a declared
one-to-one business Profile extension. Runtime owns the bearer, idempotency
key, Identity user ID, target Organization, profile relation field, transaction
boundary, and one-time credential handling.

The Profile object must already use `ux.kind=identity_profile_extension`. A
profile binding fixes `binding_key` to that extension's
`business_identity.key` and fixes `object_key` to the Profile object. Update
and disable require at least one binding because Runtime resolves the Identity
user through a locked, versioned Profile record.

Compact example (profile bindings are keyed by `object_key`):

```json
{
  "objects": {
    "employee_profile": {
      "fields": {
        "identity_user_id": "relation!->identity_user;cardinality=one_to_one",
        "employee_no": "text!;unique",
        "display_label": "text"
      },
      "ux": {
        "kind": "identity_profile_extension",
        "config": {
          "identity_relation_field": "identity_user_id",
          "cardinality": "one_to_one",
          "business_identity": {"key": "employee"},
          "default_visibility": "when_readable"
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "roles": {
    "administrator": ["employee_profile.deliver_identity;all"],
    "employee": ["employee_profile.read;owner"],
    "manager": ["employee_profile.read;all"]
  },
  "actions": {
    "employee_profile.deliver_identity": {
      "kind": "object_operation",
      "input": {
        "login_id": "email!",
        "display_name": "text!",
        "employee_no": "text!;unique",
        "role_key": "select![employee|manager]",
        "manager": "user"
      },
      "target_organization": {
        "source": "explicit",
        "input": "target_organization_id"
      },
      "output": {"initial_credential": "initial_credential"},
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Deliver the Identity user, role set, and employee Profile atomically.",
        "identity_handler_delivery": {
          "operations": ["create", "update", "disable", "resolve"],
          "profile_bindings": {
            "employee_profile": {"binding_key": "employee"}
          },
          "initial_credential_output_field": "initial_credential"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The example deliberately shows both Action-field ownership cases. `login_id`,
`display_name`, `role_key`, and `manager` are Identity-owned delivery input,
not persisted fields on `employee_profile`, so they use standalone DSL without
Object-only modifiers. For example, write `"display_name": "text!"`, not
`"display_name": "text!;max_length=120"`. A conceptual limit in Identity is
not a project Object source contract.

`employee_no` is different: it is a business Profile field persisted on the
bound `employee_profile`. Its Action input may reuse `unique` only because the
owning Object has the exact same `employee_no` key and compatible
`"text!;unique"` contract. Do not write a partial or invented copy such as
`"employee_no": "text!;max_length=64"`. If a Profile-bound Action input does
not exactly reuse a field on the owning Object or an Object in
`handler.access`, keep it standalone and remove Object-only modifiers. Never
add a fake Object field to make source inference pass.

Operations are a non-empty unique subset of `create`, `update`, `disable`, and
`resolve`. Mutation operations require `target_organization`; `owner_org_id`
is never Action input. Plane generates operation-specific methods and a typed
Profile-create DTO containing only business-owned Profile fields. The trusted
`identity_user` relation is deliberately absent and is injected by Runtime.

Create accepts login mode `none`. Login mode `password` is generated only when
`initial_credential_output_field` names an optional `initial_credential`
Action output. The Handler never supplies a password. Identity returns the
initial password in volatile memory; Runtime injects
`{initial_password,must_change_password}` only after the outer transaction
commits, marks the response no-store, and never persists or logs it.

Update and disable use explicit user and Profile expected versions. Resolve
returns only Identity's bounded projection for attribution and eligibility.
Project code must not call Identity storage or HTTP directly, forge relation
columns, accept credentials as input, or widen generated delivery methods into
generic maps.
# Identity account and business profile

Identity owns accounts, credentials, sessions, users, organization placement
and role assignments. A project models only business attributes missing from
the canonical Identity user.

Use one profile-extension Object with one one-to-one relation to the external
`identity_user`; do not copy login, display name, email, phone, locale,
timezone, status, manager or organization fields.

```json
{
  "objects": {
    "gym_member": {
      "fields": {
        "identity_user_id": "relation!->identity_user;cardinality=one_to_one",
        "membership_no": "text!;unique",
        "membership_status": "select![active:有效|frozen:冻结]=active"
      },
      "ux": {
        "kind": "identity_profile_extension",
        "config": {
          "identity_relation_field": "identity_user_id",
          "cardinality": "one_to_one",
          "business_identity": {
            "key": "gym_member",
            "status_field": "membership_status",
            "active_status_values": ["active"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "roles": {
    "member": ["gym_member.read;owner"]
  }
}
```

Relation uniqueness is expressed only as `cardinality=one_to_one`, which makes
the compiler derive `unique`. Never add the `unique` modifier to a relation.

The relation is business linkage, not an account or assignment record. Plane
expands the field and Runtime manifest; Identity resolves the
authenticated principal and current assignment at request time.

Never seed users through Blueprint, let an ordinary business Action forge
Runtime actor/workspace identity, or create a project-local login/profile
service. A declared [Identity HandlerDelivery](identity-handler-delivery.md)
Action is the narrow delivery exception: its business input may select the
Identity user values, role key, manager, and target Organization consumed by
the generated typed capability, while Runtime still supplies the authenticated
actor, Workspace, idempotency, generated user ID, trusted Profile relation,
transaction, and credential handling. Tests provision real principals and
assignments through the supported Identity path and verify allowed and denied
scopes separately.
# Actions and transactions

Use a project-owned Handler only for named business behavior that plain Runtime
CRUD cannot express: conditional rules, derived writes, multi-Object atomicity,
governed state transitions, durable external intent, or typed project logic.

## V3 Action input

```json
{
  "actions": {
    "invoice.approve": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "input": {
        "comment": "long_text!",
        "effective_date": "date!"
      },
      "output": {
        "status": "select![approved|rejected]"
      },
      "preconditions": ["status == pending"],
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Approval validates eligibility and atomically records the decision",
        "access": {
          "invoice": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
          "invoice_decision": ["create"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Action key has exactly one dot and its prefix is the owning Object. Plane
derives `object_key`, default name, audit value, same-key Permission,
`authorization.allowed_roles`, full payload/result field arrays, empty
contracts and generated Handler source identity.

Action kind also fixes invocation scope and execution ownership:

| Kind | Scope | Project Handler |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `object_create` | Object | Forbidden: Runtime-owned generic create |
| `object_operation`, `bulk_operation` | Object | Allowed for project-owned behavior |
| `record_update`, `record_delete`, `record_restore`, `transition_state`, `conditional_update`, `record_operation` | Routed record | Allowed for project-owned behavior |

When creation only maps declared fields into one ordinary Object, use
`object_create` without a Handler. When creation must derive trusted owner/org,
coordinate multiple Objects, or apply other project logic, use
`object_operation` with a Handler and its exact `access` declaration. Do not
name a Handler Action with the bare suffix `create`, `read`, `update`, `delete`,
`restore`, `import`, or `export`: those exact `<object>.<operation>` keys are
Runtime Object Permissions. Use a business verb such as `lead.register` or a
qualified key such as `lead.create_owned`, then use that exact key in Role and
workflow references.

The model must not author `object_key`, `payload_fields`, `authorization`,
`audit_event`, `handler.data_access`, `handler.output`, empty `defaults`, or
requirement behavior tuples.

`input` and `output` are keyed field-DSL maps. Omit them when empty. Relation
fields require `->target`; select fields require their stable value vocabulary.
A plain Action-only field needs no Object source. Currency and percent fields,
plus any Action field carrying Object-only DSL modifiers, ask Plane to infer a
source from the owning Object and the Objects declared in `handler.access`.
Plane uses only the Action field's exact key, preferring the owning Object over
an equally named field elsewhere in the Handler access closure. Differently
named fields are never bound through Action verbs, prefixes, suffixes, stemming,
edit distance, grammar, or synonyms. If an Action input and Object field carry
the same business datum, use the same stable key end to end—for example
`"rejection_reason": "long_text!;max_length=1000"` in the Action and
`rejection_reason` in every invocation. If the value is genuinely Action-only,
remove Object-only modifiers—for example use `"reason": "long_text"` instead
of `"reason": "long_text;max_length=1000"`. Missing or ambiguous exact-key
reuse fails with the actual DSL and a copyable replacement; compatible rename
candidates may be listed, but Plane never chooses one. Source reuse affects
generated type/lineage only and never copies an Object value into the payload.

This rule also applies to Foundation-capability input. For
`identity_handler_delivery`, Identity-owned non-Profile values such as
`login_id`, `display_name`, `role_key`, and `manager` use standalone DSL (for
example `email!`, `text!`, `select![employee|manager]`, and `user`) and must not
borrow Object-only modifiers. A business Profile value may reuse those
modifiers only from an exact same-key compatible field on the owning Object or
an Object in `handler.access`; see the complete copyable
[Identity HandlerDelivery](identity-handler-delivery.md) example.

`preconditions` is a closed Runtime expression grammar, not natural language.
The complete supported forms are:

- `field is present`
- `field in value1,value2`
- `field not in value1,value2`
- `field == value` and `field != value`
- `field > number_or_field`, `field >= number_or_field`, `field < number_or_field`, and `field <= number_or_field`
- `date_field >= today` and `date_field <= today`

For example, write `status not in converted,lost`, not “status is not converted
or lost”. Caller ownership belongs in the Role grant's `owner` data scope.
Related-record existence, cross-Object checks, and other complex conditions
belong in the source-owned Handler using the declared `handler.access`; do not
encode them as prose preconditions.

Never model `id`, `request_id`, `trace_id`, `correlation_id`,
`idempotency_key`, `workspace_id`, `principal_id`, `record_id`, `tenant_id`, or
`session_id` as Action input. Runtime supplies routed record target, actor and
workspace context; HTTP supplies request/trace/idempotency; backend code creates
technical IDs. A real order number or contract number belongs in the model
only when it is business data.

## Handler EffectAuthority

`handler.access` is keyed by Object and lists only operations the algorithm
actually uses:

- read: `get`, `get_for_update`, `optional`, `list`, `exists`, `count`;
- write: `create`, `update`, `conditional_update`, `delete`, `restore`.

Existing-record update/delete/restore requires `get_for_update` or
`conditional_update`. A friendly precheck does not replace an atomic
conditional mutation.

`handler.reason` must state the concrete business gap, not implementation
boilerplate. Plane derives involved Objects, exact read/write sets,
single-/multi-record scope, transaction requirement and rollback behavior from
access. Every written Object becomes `action_only`; all other Objects become
`direct_crud`. Direct CRUD grants or entrypoint mutation exposure on an
`action_only` Object fail model compilation.

Allowed roles are reverse-derived only from Roles that explicitly grant the
same-key Action Permission with a `data_scope`. The compiler projects the
Handler's minimum Object EffectAuthority from `handler.access`; the model does
not repeat Role scoped-Permission grants. The Handler does not bypass
authorization: generated capabilities apply `owner`/`org`/`org_child`/
`target_org` predicates and EffectAuthority inside the same host transaction;
`all` adds no data-scope predicate.

An Action may instead declare only `handler.cross_workspace_aggregates` and
omit `handler.access`. Plane derives each aggregate source Object into the
read-effect and authorization closure while keeping raw `Get`/`List` Object
APIs out of the Handler facade. The Object, fields, operations, filters, fixed
date-bucket grain/time zone, result schema, and hard limits are source-owned;
Runtime alone selects active installed Workspaces. Read
[cross-Workspace aggregates](cross-workspace-aggregates.md) before authoring
this capability.

Other capability-only Handlers may omit `handler.access` when they use only
Runtime-selected [target Organization/store delivery](organization-delivery.md),
[Identity HandlerDelivery](identity-handler-delivery.md), or
[Workspace Identity usage](workspace-identity-usage.md). Their source, operation
set, profile binding, output field, and page bounds are static model decisions.
Generated methods expose only those decisions; Runtime supplies actor,
installation scope, target ownership, transaction metadata, and other trusted
context. Do not repeat compiler-owned effect closure as raw Object access.

For every existing-record update/delete/restore, generated capabilities first
select the single ID or bounded ID batch with the exact Action scope compiled
into SQL, then retain the same non-`all` scope predicate in the atomic mutation.
Workspace and target-ID conditions remain mandatory for `all`. A mixed
allowed/out-of-scope batch fails without partial writes. Application-side
filtering is never authorization evidence.

## Connector calls and post-commit work

After the selected `email/smtp` connection is declared as `billing_email`, its
published durable operation is keyed by that connection:

```json
{"connector_calls": {"billing_email": "send_email"}}
```

Do not perform an irreversible synchronous external write inside the database
transaction. Persist a durable intent/outbox operation, commit local state,
then let the owning Integration/Notification worker deliver and reconcile it.
The Handler may return committed local evidence; it must not claim provider
success before provider evidence exists.

## Implementation sequence

1. Run `model plan`; fix the complete model diagnostic set.
2. Run `apply model`; read only the selected Action's generated context packet.
3. Implement the typed Handler with generated capabilities and one host-owned
   transaction boundary.
4. Preserve typed permission, scope, conflict and validation errors.
5. Test success, each accepted denial/conflict branch, rollback, replay and
   restart behavior required by the PRD.

Do not open a raw database handle, construct SQL, invoke Runtime over HTTP from
an embedded Handler, trust request identity fields, or manually reimplement
the generated authorization/data-scope checks.

For authoritative calculations, persist the policy identity/version, the
actual rule snapshot, the input snapshot and an ordered calculation trace with
the settled result. Never rewrite settled history after a rule change; produce
explicit reversal or adjustment entries linked to the original result.
# Permissions and data scope

Code-owned resources define the stable permission catalog. The backend model
defines application roles and business scope decisions. Identity owns users,
credentials, live assignments and principal resolution.

## Compact role input

Roles are keyed by stable identity. Each exact Permission grant carries its own
data visibility decision:

```json
{"roles": {
  "work_operator": [
    "work_item.read;owner",
    "work_item.export;org",
    "work_item_attachment.read;org_child;audit_denial"
  ]
}}
```

When a Role also needs metadata, use the extended object form and put the same
grant strings under `grants`:

```json
{"roles": {
  "work_operator": {
    "grants": [
      "work_item.read;owner",
      "work_item.export;org",
      "work_item_attachment.read;org_child;audit_denial"
    ],
    "field_permissions": {
      "work_item.private_note": {
        "read": true,
        "write": false,
        "export": false,
        "masked": true,
        "reason": "Private notes are not exportable"
      }
    }
  }
}}
```

`name` defaults from the role key. Every array item is an exact Permission key
and one of `all`, `owner`, `org`, `org_child`, or `target_org`, separated by a
semicolon. Append `;audit_denial` only when denied attempts must be audited.
Duplicate Permission keys are invalid. `grants` may be omitted from the extended
object when no explicit business grant exists.

The backend model must not declare role-level `data_scope`, `scope_overrides`,
`record_scope`, `data_permissions`,
`reference_permissions`, a root `permissions` collection, accounts, sessions,
users, assignments, or menu assignments.

## Compiler authorization closure

Plane preserves each authored scoped grant and validates the complete
authorization closure:

- `Action` -> the same-key Permission definition registered by Runtime;
- Role same-key Action grants -> the compiler-derived Action allowlist;
- explicit Object read/export/CRUD grants -> their own scoped grants;
- eligible relation fields -> exact source/field/target reference policies;
- Report and Export Control sources -> their validated functional/data closure.

The compiled Blueprint and Runtime Manifest contain only
`permissions[].permission_key/data_scope/audit_denial` for Role authorization.

A Handler-written Object is `action_only`. Its allowed roles explicitly grant
the same-key Action Permission, but do not receive direct CRUD mutation
permissions. Authoring such a direct permission is a blocking write-owner
conflict.

Field, export and guardrail policies remain explicit business exceptions and
use keyed maps wherever their schema has stable identity. Reference policies
are compiler-owned because relation target and role access are already known.
Custom data predicates are not part of role authoring. If none of the five
canonical scopes expresses the requirement, stop and surface a contract gap;
do not invent a sixth value or embed a predicate:

```json
{"roles": {"work_operator": ["work_item.read;owner"]}}
```

## Runtime ownership and verification

At apply, Plane publishes the generated project role catalog. Identity stores
current users and role assignments. Runtime evaluates the resolved principal,
exact scoped grant, field/reference policy and export policy on every
request.

Scope enforcement is storage-bound. For `all`, SQL keeps workspace, caller
filters and target IDs but adds no data-scope predicate. For the other four
values, list/read SQL combines the compiled scope predicate with caller filters;
update/delete/restore first select the requested single ID or bounded ID batch
within that scope, then retain the same predicate on the atomic mutation. Mixed
allowed/out-of-scope batches fail and roll back.
Application-side filtering of unscoped rows is never sufficient evidence.

Verification uses SDK-backed principals created through the supported Identity
test path:

- positive cases prove the exact Permission grant and matching `data_scope`;
- function-denied cases omit the permission or assignment;
- row-denied cases target a record outside the selected scope;
- rejected mutations prove durable state did not change;
- field/reference/export cases assert their exact masking or denial.

Never paste an SDK `AccessBundle`, `FunctionGrant`, or `DataPolicy` into
`backend/model/*.json`, and never provision a Blueprint user just to make a
test executable.

# In-app notifications

Runtime Notification owns the personal Inbox, unread/read/archive state,
deduplication, localized immutable copy, preferences and optional external
delivery. Use it only for durable user-impacting events with resolvable users;
validation errors, logs and operator incidents stay with their owning module.

Prefer built-in events from Workflow, Scheduler, Integration, batch and Report
owners. A project-owned Handler declares only the event type it may dispatch;
it does not render copy, choose arbitrary URLs or create an Inbox table.

Select the `notifications` topic in the one reading-plan request and consume
its inlined `notification.delivery_governance` machine contract before
authoring project event types or delivery rules. Consume the inlined
`notification.templates` contract only when the accepted requirement includes
an external delivery template. Do not issue separate per-category capability
calls; `notification` is the module key, not a selectable category key.

        "reason": "Assignment and its recipient notification intent must commit atomically",
        "access": {"ticket": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"]},
        "notification_event_types": ["ticket.assigned"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Every locale placeholder must exist in the keyed `variables` DSL map. Every
semantic action is keyed once, uses `resource_type: project_record`, declares
one semantic route key, and has a localized label in every locale. Persisted
actions are semantic references, never literal URLs or HTTP requests.

Every project event type named by any project-owned
`actions.<action>.handler.notification_event_types` entry must publish at least
one keyed semantic action with `resource_type: project_record` and a non-empty
`route_key`. This is required even when the notification copy itself is valid:
the Inbox must have a safe project-record destination. Select the route from
the accepted frontend navigation contract; never infer a route key from the
event key, Action key, Object key, or URL. `model plan` reports every missing
event/Action pair together.

Notification variables use only `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `email`,
`number`, `text`, or `url` plus optional `!`. They are interpolation values, not
business-schema fields, so they do not accept options, defaults, relations, or
modifiers. Keep a controlled vocabulary on its owning Object/Action and expose
its notification placeholder as `text!`; for example replace
`select![approved|rejected]` with `text!` here.

`notification_templates` is only for external `email`, `collaboration`, or
`whatsapp` delivery; there is no `in_app` template channel. External delivery
failure does not undo an already committed Inbox item.

Generated Handler capabilities accept exact recipient user IDs, a stable
source-event/deduplication identity, subject Object/record/version,
occurrence time and typed variables. Runtime validates the declared grant and
stages the intent in the same transaction as the real business mutation.
Notification-only Actions fail closed.

Acceptance proves the source event, intended recipient, no
cross-user leakage, durable Inbox state, unread reconciliation, safe semantic
action resolution and replay deduplication. A stream event is only a refresh
signal, not persistence evidence.

Inventory every materialized managed verification actor before finalizing
Roles. In a model with `mandatory_in_app:true` events, each provisioned human
actor must include `notification.inbox.list;all`, including an
acceptance/admin Role used only to provision fixtures, deliver identities, or
run verification. Such a Role still needs the grant when it is not a business notification recipient;
do not limit the actor inventory to Roles named by the notification requirement.

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "sales_rep": ["lead.read;org", "notification.inbox.list;all"],
    "crm_acceptance_admin": ["sales_profile.deliver_identity;all", "notification.inbox.list;all"]
  }
}
```

This is the exact executable Permission for
`GET /notification/inbox`; an event declaration, recipient identity, business
Object read grant, or successful login does not authorize the route. Canonical
scope `all` selects Notification's route policy and does not bypass the Inbox's
authenticated-user/workspace mailbox isolation. Resolve other Inbox operations
from the implementation packet route index and grant their exact
`required_role_grant.compact` only to actors that exercise them.
# Organization unit

Identity owns one organization tree. Company, division, region, store,
department, team and warehouse are node types in that tree, not separate
project hierarchies. Runtime consumes Identity-expanded organization and
reporting descendants.

## Organization-only decision rule

Use `identity_organization_unit` whenever a hierarchy primarily expresses one
or more of these concerns:

- a user's primary organization placement;
- management or operating responsibility;
- organization-based data scope;
- approval, escalation or operational routing;
- a stable operating structure inside one workspace.

Industry terminology does not justify a second domain hierarchy.
Headquarters, regions, stores, branches, factories, campuses, hospitals,
clinics, hotels and service centers remain organization units when they carry
the responsibilities above. Do not author headquarters, region, restaurant,
store, branch, warehouse, factory, campus, hospital,
organization-membership or hierarchy-mapping Objects merely to reproduce an
organization tree.

## Common organization topologies

| Scenario | Organization tree |
| --- | --- |
| Restaurant, retail, pharmacy, coffee or gym chain | Headquarters -> region -> city area -> store |
| Corporate administration | Group/company -> division -> department -> team |
| Sales organization | Headquarters -> sales division -> region -> city team |
| Warehousing and logistics | Headquarters -> region -> warehouse |
| Mixed organization | Regions, stores, warehouses, departments and teams under one headquarters |
| Multi-company group | Group company -> subsidiary -> division -> department |

A restaurant business may use one mixed tree:

```text
总部 (company)
├── 上海区域 (region)
│   ├── 浦东片区 (region)
│   │   ├── 前楼店 (store)
│   │   └── 世纪大道店 (store)
│   └── 上海中心仓 (warehouse)
└── 运营事业部 (division)
    ├── 采购部 (department)
    └── 门店督导组 (team)
```

Repeated node types are valid when the business has several regional levels.
`总部` is normally the name of a `company` node, not a separate node type.

Other organization-shaped structures include bank or insurance headquarters,
branches and outlets; manufacturing factories and workshops; education
campuses; hospitals and clinics; engineering or property-management project
departments and service centers; and hotels. When a required organization
node type is absent from the release-bound Identity or administration
vocabulary, preserve the organization requirement and report an Identity
node-type capability gap. Do not work around the gap by creating a Blueprint
business Object or by selecting an inaccurate node type.

Use one tree for a multi-company group only when its companies share the same
workspace and management boundary. Each independently isolated data and
management boundary is one separate workspace; do not add a tenant Object or
table beside it.

## Boundary with business Objects

A business Object is justified only by an independent business aggregate with
its own facts, lifecycle, commands or transaction rules. It may relate to
`identity_organization_unit`, but it must not copy the organization parent,
path, membership or authorization hierarchy. Pure geography, brands,
independent partners, customer organizations, temporary matrix assignments,
contracts, inventory, equipment, menus and delivery projects are not
automatically organization nodes. A project department used for personnel
placement and authorization may be an organization unit; the delivery project
with its contract, schedule, cost and lifecycle remains a business Object.

Projects may store a business relation to the canonical external Object:

```json
{
  "objects": {
    "delivery_project": {
      "fields": {
        "responsible_org_id": "relation->identity_organization_unit"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Do not target retired department entities or copy parent, path, ancestor,
manager or depth columns. A domain-specific store/warehouse Object is valid
only for an independent business aggregate as described above, relates back
to the Identity node and never recreates the organization tree.

Every exact Role Permission carries its own explicit scope:

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "operator": ["service_request.read;org_child"]
  }
}
```

The only scopes are `all`, `owner`, `org`, `org_child`, and `target_org`.
`target_org` uses the trusted support-organization scope supplied by Identity.
Omitting the exact Permission denies access; do not add custom scopes or predicates.

Every business record receives Runtime-owned `owner_user_id` and
`owner_org_id`. Do not declare them, `scope_owner`, organization expansion or
reporting paths in the backend model. Runtime initializes ownership from the
trusted principal and Identity evaluates the current tree on each request.
These system columns exist only behind Runtime's storage and authorization
boundary: they are not project-declarable fields and cannot appear in Object
SQL or Report `result_schema`. An `owner`, `org`, `org_child`, or `target_org`
Report is scoped by Runtime before query execution; its SQL does not select,
filter, join, group, or order by either ownership column.
# Target Organization and store delivery

Use `target_organization` when every business mutation in one project-owned
Handler must have the same Runtime-selected `owner_org_id`. The Handler never
accepts or writes `owner_org_id`; Runtime resolves one immutable target before
the first mutation and rejects any conflicting ownership.

The source is closed:

- `explicit` is valid only on an object Action. Set `input` to
  `target_organization_id`; this value is Runtime invocation metadata and is
  not a Handler payload field.
- `record_owner` is valid only on a record Action. Runtime resolves the target
  from the anchor record's owner.
- `provisioned_store` is valid only on an object Action. The Handler must call
  the generated store provision capability in the same UoW before business
  mutations. Runtime and Identity create the store Organization and retain its
  opaque ID as the Action target.

Compact provision example:

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "administrator": ["store_config.provision;org_child"]
  },
  "actions": {
    "store_config.provision": {
      "kind": "object_operation",
      "target_organization": {"source": "provisioned_store"},
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Provision one store Organization and its configuration atomically.",
        "access": {"store_config": ["create"]},
        "store_organization_catalog": {"max_page_size": 25}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`store_organization_catalog` is a separate optional read capability. Its
`max_page_size` is required and must be 1 through 100. Generated requests have
only `page_size` and opaque `cursor`; Workspace, actor, Organization scope,
Identity token, hierarchy traversal, and authorization are Runtime-owned. The
fixed result is `id`, `code`, `name`, `status`, `parent_organization_id`,
`sort_order`, `version`, and `next_cursor`.

Project code uses only the generated `TargetOrganization.Resolve`,
`StoreOrganizations.Provision`, and `StoreOrganizations.List` methods present
in its Action context. It cannot enumerate arbitrary Organizations, select a
different target after resolution, or inject a physical Workspace identity.

## Store settings rename and disable

Grant Identity store mutations separately and exactly on a record Action:

```json
{
  "actions": {
    "store_config.update_settings": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "target_organization": {"source": "record_owner"},
      "input": {
        "store_name": "text!;max_length=200",
        "expected_store_version": "integer!;min=1",
        "expected_record_version": "integer!",
        "theme": "text!"
      },
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Rename the Identity store and update business settings atomically with independent CAS tokens.",
        "access": {"store_config": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"]},
        "store_organization_mutations": ["rename"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`rename` generates only `StoreOrganizations.Rename`; `disable` generates only
`StoreOrganizations.Disable`. Runtime derives the Organization from the anchor
record owner. The browser supplies no Organization ID and never calls Identity
directly. `expected_store_version` protects the Identity Organization, while
the business record uses its own compare-and-set token. Returning either error
rolls back the whole Action UoW; retrying the same Action idempotency identity
replays the committed result.

For legacy imports, require an explicit operator-approved mapping from every
legacy Workspace/store row to a Runtime Workspace and Identity store
Organization. Never infer by code, display name, row order, or the first match.
An unmapped or ambiguous row must stop migration for adjudication. After a
mapping is approved, the legacy `store_config.name` may seed the Identity store
name exactly once; it is not retained as a parallel business-owned name field.
# Project role and data-scope cookbook

The backend model defines business roles and a scope on every exact Permission;
Plane derives reference policies;
Identity owns users and live role assignments.

Use exactly these scopes. Choose from the business ownership boundary, not from
the screen name or the role's seniority:

| Scope | Runtime row boundary | Use it for | Do not use it for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | No additional data-scope predicate inside the current workspace. Workspace, caller filter and target-ID predicates still apply. | A workspace-wide responsibility, such as a central finance operator processing every invoice, an auditor reading every business record, or a shared catalog maintained for the whole workspace. | A convenient default when ownership is unclear, or access intended to cross workspace boundaries. |
| `owner` | `owner_user_id == current subject ID`. | Individually owned work, such as a salesperson's assigned leads, a member's own profile or booking, or a handler that may update only the target record assigned to its actor. | “Created by me” unless creator and current owner are deliberately the same fact; team, manager-reporting-line, or organization access. |
| `org` | `owner_org_id == current subject org ID`. | One-node organization responsibility, such as store staff operating only their own store's orders or a department clerk handling only that department's requests. | Regional managers who also need descendant organizations, or support staff serving another organization. |
| `org_child` | `owner_org_id` is in the Identity-issued current-organization subtree (`org_scope_ids`). | Hierarchical line responsibility, such as a regional manager seeing the region plus child stores, or a division operator processing its departments' records. | Direct-report/team membership—the scope follows the organization tree, not the personnel reporting line—or a separately supported target organization. |
| `target_org` | `owner_org_id` is in the Identity-issued trusted support-organization subtree (`support_org_scope_ids`). | Cross-organization service responsibility, such as a shared-service or customer-support agent whose real home organization remains unchanged but who is assigned to serve a sales/customer organization and its descendants. | Arbitrary cross-organization access, the actor's home organization tree, or an organization ID selected from the request. Without a trusted support assignment the scope matches no rows. |

Apply the choice independently to every exact Action Permission. A role may,
for example, read all department requests with `org_child` but approve only
personally assigned requests with `owner`. For scoped create or reassignment,
the resulting Runtime-owned `owner_user_id` or `owner_org_id` must remain inside
that Permission's selected boundary.

## `target_org` functional-service patterns

Use `target_org` when a functional-service actor keeps one real home
organization but is responsible for data owned by another business
organization subtree. Keep the current contract names distinct:

- `org_id` is the user's real primary organization;
- `support_org_id` is the optional Identity-managed root of the business
  organization subtree that the user serves;
- Identity validates that root and derives it plus its active descendants into
  the trusted `support_org_scope_ids` principal fact;
- `target_org` is the data-scope value on each exact Permission and compiles to
  the derived support subtree.

There is no `target_org_id` field. Do not change the user's primary `org_id`,
attach the user to a manager account or Role, copy organization paths into
business records, or author live user bindings in the backend model. The
Identity administrator assigns `support_org_id` to an active organization-unit
node.

### Customer service reading sales-owned customers

Assume customer records are owned by the sales organization through their
Runtime `owner_org_id`. A customer-service agent belongs to the Customer
Service organization, so `org` and `org_child` correctly provide no customer
access. Keep the agent's `org_id` as Customer Service, set `support_org_id` to
the organization-unit node led by the responsible Sales Manager or Sales
Director (or another truthful sales-region root), and grant only the needed
exact Action:

```json
{"roles": {"customer_service": ["customer.read;target_org"]}}
```

The agent can then read customers whose `owner_org_id` belongs to that sales
subtree. This does not grant `customer.update`, export, or any other Action, and
does not make Customer Service the owner of those customers. “One agent serves
many customers” is represented by those customers' sales-owner nodes falling
under the assigned support subtree, not by listing customer IDs on the user.

### HR account administration for different operating teams

Assume two HR account administrators both belong to an HR operations
organization, but one manages Customer Service accounts and the other manages
Sales accounts. Keep both administrators' real `org_id` in HR. Assign the first
administrator's `support_org_id` to the Customer Service organization root and
the second administrator's to the Sales organization root. Give each HR role
the exact Identity Actions required by the workflow, for example:

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "scoped_account_admin": [
      "identity.organization_units.list;target_org",
      "identity.users.list;target_org",
      "identity.users.get;target_org",
      "identity.users.create;target_org"
    ]
  }
}
```

Identity then returns organization nodes whose IDs are in that administrator's
support subtree, returns users whose `org_id` is in the same subtree, and
rejects creation of a user whose `org_id` falls outside it. Add update, disable,
role-assignment, credential or security Actions only when the requirements call
for them; list/create scope never implies those grants.

The current user model has one `support_org_id`, so it expresses one connected
organization subtree. If one actor must serve several unrelated roots, do not
silently use `all` or invent a list-valued field: use a truthful common parent
node when the organization model has one, otherwise surface a contract gap.

There is no `none` or `custom` scope. Absence of an exact Permission grant means deny.
This example scopes member records to Runtime-maintained ownership:

```json
{
  "objects": {
    "gym_member": {
      "fields": {
        "identity_user_id": "relation!->identity_user;cardinality=one_to_one",
        "status": "select![active:有效|frozen:冻结]=active"
      }
    },
    "booking": {"fields": {"member_id": "relation!->gym_member"}}
  },
  "roles": {
    "member": ["gym_member.read;owner", "booking.read;owner", "booking.create;owner"],
    "front_desk": ["gym_member.read;all", "booking.read;all", "booking.update;all"]
  },
  "entrypoints": {
    "member_booking": {
      "audience": "consumer",
      "primary_object": "booking",
      "read_objects": ["gym_member", "booking"],
      "create_objects": ["booking"]
    },
    "front_desk": {
      "audience": "internal",
      "primary_object": "booking",
      "read_objects": ["gym_member", "booking"],
      "update_objects": ["booking"]
    }
  }
}
```

Plane preserves every exact scoped grant. Runtime exposes an entrypoint only
when the exact Permission and its row scope pass. Tests provision real Identity principals and prove positive,
function-denied and out-of-scope cases, including unchanged durable state after
rejected writes.

Never author Identity users, assignments, SDK access bundles, ownership system
columns, wildcard permissions or an application-side authorization service.
# Records, fields, and relations

Runtime owns ordinary record persistence, typed normalization, validation,
references, queries and mutations. The backend model declares only business
Objects and their business fields.

## Compact Object form

```json
{"objects": {
  "invoice": {
    "description": "Customer invoice and governed financial state",
    "fields": {
      "business_no": "text!;unique",
      "status": "select![draft:草稿|issued:已开具]=draft",
      "customer_id": "relation!->customer",
      "amount": "currency!=0;precision=19;scale=2;currency=CNY;rounding=half_even",
      "discount_rate": "percent;precision=5;scale=2;rounding=half_even",
      "remark": "long_text;max_length=500"
    }
  }
}}
```

Object identity and field identity are their map keys. Plane supplies default
names, required empty config, labeled options and deterministic Object
description when no meaningful explicit description is present.

Supported types are `boolean`, `currency`, `date`, `datetime`, `email`,
`integer`, `long_text`, `number`, `percent`, `phone`, `relation`, `select`,
`text`, `url`, and `user`. `number` is binary floating point. Use `currency` or
`percent` for exact declared-scale values; generated code keeps their canonical
named decimal strings.

Exact values use `precision`, `scale`, `currency`, and `rounding`. `relation`
requires `->target` and cannot have a default. `select` requires a stable,
unique vocabulary; `value:label` carries localized display text without
changing the stored value. Supported validators are `min_length`, `max_length`,
`min`, `max`, and `pattern`. `unique` is a non-relation flag with no value;
relations must use `cardinality=one_to_one` and let the compiler derive unique.
`indexed` and `localized` are flags. Relation modifiers are `cardinality`,
`on_delete`, and `inverse`; select fields may reference `dictionary` or
`value_domain` instead of repeating a vocabulary.

Defaults must appear before the first modifier, for example
`currency!=0;precision=19`. Field types, modifier names and closed platform
enum values accept mixed case and compile to the documented lowercase form;
ISO currency codes compile to uppercase. Identity-bearing keys, relation
targets and select values remain strict lowercase identifiers.

The grammar is closed. Unknown types, modifiers, duplicates, invalid regexes,
bad numeric arguments, relation defaults and select defaults outside the
vocabulary fail model loading.

Runtime owns record `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, workspace identity and
ownership columns. Never redeclare them as Object fields. Use a business key
such as `business_no`, `submitted_at`, or `effective_date` when that value is
part of the domain.

Foundation entities may be relation targets only when their published Runtime
capability allows it. Do not copy a Foundation Object into project metadata.

## Dictionaries

Use inline select values for a small stable vocabulary. Use a Dictionary only
when several fields share localized/orderable/activatable vocabulary:

```json
{
  "dictionaries": {
    "case_category": {
      "items": {
        "billing": {"label": "Billing", "sort_order": 10, "status": "active"},
        "service": {"label": "Service", "sort_order": 20, "status": "active"}
      }
    }
  },
  "objects": {
    "service_case": {
      "fields": {"category": "select!;dictionary=case_category"}
    }
  }
}
```

Prefer an Object plus relation when a value has its own identity, attributes,
lifecycle, authorization or Actions. Use text only for genuinely open values.

## Ownership and data

An Object written by Handler access is automatically `action_only`; all other
Objects are `direct_crud`. The model never authors `config.write_policy`.

Baseline records are Runtime-owned and deterministic. Scenario fixtures belong
under `backend/tests/**` and use generated Runtime APIs. Never author
`seed_data`, `seed_records`, `demo_users`, repeated field keys, comma-separated
relation IDs, or direct persistence bypasses.
# CRUD and state machines

Runtime owns ordinary single-record CRUD. Use a state machine only when a
stored state field has a closed transition graph; use a project Handler when a
named transition contains business rules or coordinated writes.

## Compact V3 authoring

Plane derives `direct_crud` for Objects not written by a Handler and
`action_only` for Handler-written Objects. Never author `config.write_policy`
or a CRUD behavior tuple.

```json
{
  "objects": {
    "work_item": {
      "fields": {
        "title": "text!",
        "status": "select![draft:草稿|active:处理中|retired:已结束]=draft"
      }
    }
  },
  "roles": {
    "work_operator": [
      "work_item.read;all",
      "work_item.activate;owner",
      "work_item.retire;owner"
    ]
  },
  "actions": {
    "work_item.activate": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Activation validates eligibility before changing state",
        "access": {"work_item": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"]}
      }
    },
    "work_item.retire": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Retirement records the governed terminal transition",
        "access": {"work_item": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"]}
      }
    }
  },
  "state_machines": {
    "work_item_lifecycle": {
      "object_key": "work_item",
      "field_key": "status",
      "states": ["draft", "active", "retired"],
      "terminal_states": ["retired"],
      "transitions": {
        "draft->active": "work_item.activate",
        "active->retired": "work_item.retire"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The map identity of each transition is `<from>-><to>`, making duplicate edges
structurally impossible. Every endpoint must occur in `states`; every
non-terminal state needs an outgoing edge; states must match the field's stable
select vocabulary. An Action or Workflow reference is an association, not
implicit execution: the Handler performs the write and Runtime validates the
edge.

An initial business state belongs in the field DSL default, not only in
acceptance prose. Illegal transitions fail without changing durable state.
Multi-Object transitions stay in one Handler transaction. Waiting or human
approval belongs to a Workflow whose Action node invokes the Handler.

Do not invent transition effects, patches, `from_state`/`to_state` Action
fields, or project-local lifecycle enforcement. If the active Blueprint cannot
publish required append-only, soft-delete or immutable-after-state policy,
record that exact Runtime/Blueprint gap.

# Reports

Reports read accepted domain facts; they do not create, settle or recalculate
those facts. Use governed `object_sql_v1`. If the active compiler cannot express
a truthful requirement, record a Runtime Report gap instead of adding another
query language or project endpoint.

## Compact V3 authoring

Put SQL in exactly `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`. The model references the
file once; Plane validates the canonical project-local path, normalizes line
endings, hashes it and embeds the full SQL contract.

```json
{
  "objects": {
    "customer": {"fields": {"name": "text!", "status": "select![active|inactive]"}}
  },
  "roles": {
    "customer_report_reader": {
      "grants": [
        "customer.read;org_child",
        "report.query.execute;all"
      ],
      "field_permissions": {
        "customer.name": {"read": true, "write": false, "export": false},
        "customer.status": {"read": true, "write": false, "export": false}
      }
    }
  },
  "reports": {
    "customer_names": {
      "audience_roles": ["customer_report_reader"],
      "object_sql_v1": {
        "sql_file": "backend/reports/customer_names.sql",
        "parameters": {"status": "text!"},
        "timeout_milliseconds": 5000,
        "time_zone": "UTC"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Never repeat Report, parameter or result-column keys and never declare both
`sql` and `sql_file`. Plane derives the exact `source_objects` from the parsed
`FROM`/`JOIN` tree and proves JOIN cardinality from the project JSON Object
relations and unique fields. Do not author `source_objects` or
`join_cardinalities`. Give every source an alias, every selected expression a
stable unique alias, bind only declared `:parameters`, avoid
`SELECT *`, and use deterministic ordering plus a literal bounded `LIMIT` for
multi-row results.

Parameter map values use compact field DSL with only `text`, `integer`,
`number`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `date`, or `datetime` (for example
`"from_time": "datetime!"`). Object-field types such as `select`, `relation`,
and `currency` are not SQL parameter types.

Every Object SQL business-field reference must name a field explicitly declared
in that source Object's project JSON `fields`. Runtime-owned `owner_user_id` and
`owner_org_id` must not appear in SQL or `result_schema`. The record-envelope `id` may be used internally
in JOIN predicates, filters, ordering, and `COUNT`/`COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`, but a
raw ID value must not be returned as a SELECT result. Runtime
applies owner and organization permission scope before executing the query; do
not select those internal columns to make authorization work. Each
optional `result_schema` key is only a semantic override for an existing SELECT
alias, not a way to expose an undeclared storage column.

Plane derives result keys, types, precision, scale, and order from SELECT. If a
business meaning differs from the default, author only the needed
`result_schema.<alias>` override; overrides bind by alias, never by JSON or
lexical key order.

Quote every model-derived Object and field identifier with MySQL backticks:
write ``FROM `lead` l`` and ``JOIN `order` o``; for qualified fields, write
``l.`status``` while keeping the alias `l` plain. This is mandatory even for
ordinary stable keys because parser-keyword classification is not an authoring
choice. Keep aliases, parameter names, and result aliases as unquoted stable
keys.

Object SQL is one read-only select tree. The current authoring compiler does
not support CTEs, subqueries, unions or window functions. Persist historical
snapshots/ledgers rather than recomputing history from current settings.

Every Report uses `object_sql_v1`, including interactive summaries,
materialized snapshots, and batch exports. Its selected columns, ordering, and
literal row bound are explicit and compiler-checked.

When overriding an inferred type, the complete
`result_schema.<column>.type` vocabulary is `text`, `integer`,
`number`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, and `currency`. These are
query-result types, not Object field types. Object `phone`, `select`, `email`,
`long_text`, `relation`, `url`, and `user` fields project as `text`; Object
`percent` projects as `decimal`. In particular, declare a selected phone or
select column as `{"type":"text","kind":"dimension"}`.

Write any result `type` and `kind` overrides in lowercase, especially `currency`.
Plane accepts mixed-case enum input for compatibility and canonicalizes it to
the documented lowercase value before validation.

The complete optional `result_schema.<column>.kind` vocabulary is only
`dimension` and `measure`. The compiler defaults non-aggregates to `dimension`
and aggregates to `measure`; override only for real business semantics.
`metric` is not a result kind. The `report.business` capability publishes the
complete SQL/parameter/result/join contract as machine contract `object_sql_v1`.

Every audience role needs explicit `field_permissions` with `read:true` for
each business field used anywhere in the compiled plan (projection, join,
filter, grouping, or ordering), in addition to the source Object read grant.
Exporting roles also set `export:true` on that same complete field set.

Every `audience_roles` entry also needs the Report query route's exact
executable grant `report.query.execute;all`. `*.read;<scope>` determines which
source rows are visible and field policy determines which source fields are
usable; neither grants `POST /report/{reportKey}/query`. Keep a negative role
outside `audience_roles` and without `report.query.execute` when the requirement
needs a query-denial proof.

Exports are always offline through Runtime Report plus Data Exchange. For every
accepted export requirement, author a Blueprint `report_export_controls` entry
that references the Report and its source Objects and declares the required
`audit_object`, `download_object`, complete `record_mapping`, bounded `max_rows`
and business `reason`; add masking, approval, watermark, assurance,
and sensitive-field policy bindings when the requirement needs them. The two
record Objects and exporting roles must carry the exact requester-owned prepare,
audit, download, source-read and source-export grant closure reported by
`model plan`. Select the `reports` topic and, when export is required, the
`report-export` topic in the one reading-plan request. Consume their inlined
`report.business` and `records.export` machine contracts before authoring the
Report or its Runtime export operation; do not issue separate per-category
capability calls. `report_export_controls` is a Blueprint collection emitted
and checked by `model plan`; it is not a selectable capability category key.
Data Exchange is execution-only: there is likewise no `data_exchange` or
`data_exchange.jobs` authoring category.

The `report.business` capability output includes the machine-readable compact
map-value schema as contract `report_export_controls`. The surrounding map key
is the control identity, so do not repeat `key`. This complete Feature fragment
is the smallest copyable closure (the SQL file contains

The compiler derives `source_objects` on the control from the referenced

mapping fields may be omitted together with their optional Object fields.
`finance_viewer` intentionally lacks both `<source>.export` and
`report.exports.prepare`; use it for the required denial and unchanged-state
case. Do not broaden audit/download grants beyond `owner` merely to make an
export pass.

Submit the governed export, retain the returned job identity and use the
published typed job/list/download operations. Do not add export Actions,
project-owned export orchestration, synchronous CSV branches, browser-side
authoritative CSV, or a second query. The Blueprint control and its audit/
